body:
> From the second-pass review of PR #151 (#148, merged). `hkb up` rechecks `pidAlive` 300 ms after the spawn and prints "serve exited immediately (pid N) — see .kanban/logs/serve.log" — but it still pushes the process into `started`, adds no error field under `--json`, and **returns 0**. Measured: `hkb up --serve --port 80 --json` → exit 0, `started:["serve"]`, `serve.running:false`. A script sees a clean run for a board that is not up.

## What

- `src/up.js` (~121, ~158-165): a child that is dead at the recheck goes into `failed: [{ name, pid, log }]`, not `started`; exit 1 when `failed` is non-empty — mirroring what `down` already does. Human line unchanged. Pure decision in `src/model.js` beside `startDecision`.
- While there: `down` on a pid file naming a dead pid says "not running" and leaves the file — remove it; a kill that throws `ESRCH` (died between `processState` and `kill`) counts as stopped, not failed.
- Wiki page `features/up-and-down.md`: the `--json` shape gains `failed`.

## Done when

- `hkb up --serve --port 80 --json` (port refused) exits 1 with `failed:[{name:"serve",…,log:".kanban/logs/serve.log"}]` and `started:[]`; the loop half still starts and is reported.
- `test/up.test.js` covers the dead-at-recheck path and the ESRCH race. `npm run lint && npm test` green.

## Contract

- Keep `up` idempotent and non-supervising; this changes only what it reports and its exit code.
goal: hkb up reports a child that exited within the recheck window as failed, with the log path and a non-zero exit, under both human and --json output
title: hkb up exits 0 and reports started when the child died on startup
